decisive_items: a large, well-circumscribed, expansile, heterogeneous (mixed-density) mass occupying the entire left maxillary sinus
deviation and destruction of the nasal septum, invaded the ethmoid sinus, thinned, displaced, and perforated the anterior wall of the sphenoid sinus
extreme postero-superior displacement of the second molar toward the inferior orbital fissure
response.rationale: The imaging shows an aggressive, expansile mass with bony destruction and extension into pterygopalatine fossa and nasopharynx, typical of juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma in a prepubertal male. Fibrous dysplasia is less destructive and usually ground-glass; odontogenic myxoma is less likely to invade sinuses and fissures this extensively.

rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia typically presents as a painless bony expansion with ground-glass radiopacity, not a heterogeneous destructive mass with perforation and fissure involvement.
Odontogenic myxoma may cause tooth mobility but lacks the aggressive sinonasal invasion and nasopharyngeal compromise seen here.
